quick: 4 mg IV over >=15 min (oncology); 5 mg IV yearly for osteoporosis (Reclast)
Not relevant (IV); ensure hydration before infusion
Avoid - can cause fetal harm; not for women of childbearing potential unless necessary
Contraindicated/avoid if CrCl <35 (osteoporosis); reduce in oncology; do not use if severe
Serum creatinine before each dose, calcium, vitamin D, dental exam
summary: Zoledronic acid is a potent intravenous nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. The 4 mg oncology formulation treats hypercalcemia of malignancy and bone metastases/multiple myeloma; the 5 mg formulation (Reclast) treats osteoporosis once yearly. Key risks are renal toxicity, hypocalcemia, acute-phase flu-like reaction, osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures.
indications: Hypercalcemia of malignancy (albumin-corrected serum calcium >=12 mg/dL)
Patients with multiple myeloma and documented bone metastases from solid tumors, with standard antineoplastic therapy (prostate cancer must have progressed after at least one hormonal therapy)
Osteoporosis treatment/prevention and Paget disease (5 mg formulation; not for hypercalcemia or non-tumor hypercalcemia)

dosage.d: 4 mg single IV infusion over no less than 15 minutes
dosage.n: Retreat after >=7 days if calcium re-rises

dosage.d: 4 mg IV over >=15 minutes every 3-4 weeks (if CrCl >60 mL/min)
dosage.n: Add oral calcium 500 mg + vitamin D 400 IU daily

dosage.d: Reduce dose per baseline CrCl (e.g., 50-60: 3.5 mg; 40-49: 3.3 mg; 30-39: 3.0 mg)
5 mg IV once yearly over >=15 minutes

admin: Administer as a single IV infusion over no less than 15 minutes through a separate vented infusion line
Do not allow contact with calcium or other divalent cation-containing solutions (e.g., Ringer's lactate)
Adequately rehydrate the patient before infusion, especially in hypercalcemia of malignancy
Coadminister oral calcium 500 mg and vitamin D 400 IU daily for myeloma/bone metastases (correct hypocalcemia first)
Inspect for particulate matter; check serum creatinine before each dose
moa: Zoledronic acid binds avidly to hydroxyapatite in mineralized bone. As a nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate it inhibits the enzyme farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase in the mevalonate pathway, disrupting osteoclast cytoskeleton and survival. It inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption and tumor-induced calcium release, lowering serum calcium and reducing skeletal complications.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to zoledronic acid or any component (including reported anaphylaxis/angioedema)
Severe renal impairment / acute renal failure (osteoporosis: CrCl <35 mL/min)
relative: Uncorrected vitamin D deficiency or low calcium
Active dental/jaw disease or planned invasive dental procedures
Concurrent use of the 5 mg (Reclast) and 4 mg products together

preg: Avoid in pregnancy; bisphosphonates can cause fetal harm and persist in bone. Not for use in women of childbearing potential unless clearly necessary; counsel about fetal risk and contraception.
lact: It is not known whether zoledronic acid passes into human milk. Because of potential serious adverse effects, do not breastfeed during therapy.
renal: Renal toxicity, including acute renal failure, can occur; risk rises with dehydration, nephrotoxic drugs, rapid infusion and pre-existing impairment. Check serum creatinine before each dose, do not exceed 4 mg, infuse over >=15 minutes, reduce the oncology dose for CrCl 30-60 mL/min and avoid in severe impairment (and CrCl <35 mL/min for osteoporosis).
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is recommended for hepatic impairment; clinical experience is limited.

major: Nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, amphotericin) - additive renal toxicity
Loop diuretics - increased hypocalcemia and renal risk through dehydration
Other bisphosphonates / concurrent Reclast - do not combine
moderate: Aminoglycosides and calcitonin - additive lowering of serum calcium
Thalidomide (in myeloma) - may increase renal dysfunction risk
Anti-angiogenic agents - may increase osteonecrosis of the jaw risk
minor: Calcium/antacids (oral) - separate from infusion (incompatible IV with divalent cations)
interactions.food: Not applicable (IV); ensure adequate hydration around dosing.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum calcium and phosphate; may transiently raise creatinine; monitor calcium, phosphate, magnesium and renal function.

common: Flu-like acute-phase reaction (fever, myalgia, arthralgia, headache) after first infusion
emergency: Osteonecrosis of the jaw with infection

monitoring: Serum creatinine before each dose (withhold for renal deterioration)
Serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium and potassium; correct hypocalcemia and vitamin D deficiency before dosing
Dental examination and preventive dentistry before therapy; avoid invasive dental procedures during treatment
Signs of thigh/groin pain (atypical femoral fracture) on long-term use
counsel: Drink plenty of fluids before and after the infusion
Take daily calcium and vitamin D supplements as advised
Flu-like symptoms (fever, aches) may occur in the first 1-3 days and usually settle; paracetamol can help
Maintain good oral hygiene; have a dental check before treatment and report any jaw pain, swelling or loose teeth
Report new or unusual thigh, hip or groin pain (possible atypical fracture)
pk: Triphasic; long terminal release from bone (years)
Prolonged skeletal effect; oncology dosing every 3-4 weeks, osteoporosis yearly
Store at 25 C; excursions 15-30 C; discard unused portion
pearls: Osteonecrosis of the jaw - arrange a dental exam and complete invasive dental work before starting; avoid extractions during therapy
Renal toxicity is dose- and infusion-rate dependent: check creatinine each dose, infuse over >=15 minutes, do not exceed 4 mg, hydrate well
Correct hypocalcemia and vitamin D deficiency before dosing; supplement calcium/vitamin D in myeloma/bone metastases
First infusion commonly causes a transient flu-like acute-phase reaction
Do not co-administer with calcium-containing IV solutions; use a separate vented line
missed: For yearly osteoporosis dosing, schedule the missed dose as soon as possible and resume yearly administration from that date. For oncology dosing, the treatment team reschedules per protocol; do not self-administer.
overdose: Overdose (or excessive dose/rapid infusion) may cause clinically significant renal impairment, hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia and hypomagnesemia. Monitor and correct electrolytes with IV calcium gluconate, phosphate and magnesium as needed, and provide supportive renal care; there is no specific antidote.
